sources.title: Iran's Khuzestan: Thirst and Turmoil
sources.temporal_coverage: 2021 protests and preceding water-sector conditions, reported in 2023
sources.methodology: Accessible publisher summary describes the Khuzestan protest and water-scarcity analysis; detailed methods are not stated there.
sources.limitations: The canonical publisher page returned 403; claims are limited to the indexed publisher summary, not full-report detail.

sources.title: Groundwater resources exploitation management in response to water scarcity challenges in Khuzestan Province, Iran
sources.organization: Journal of Groundwater Science and Engineering
sources.temporal_coverage: Groundwater measurements from 2008-2018; article published in 2025
sources.methodology: Analyzes groundwater levels and quality from 204 pumping wells and 70 piezometric wells across 19 aquifers using hydrochemical and GIS methods.
sources.limitations: Well observations cover 2008-2018; findings do not measure current household access or climate attribution.

sources.title: Iran's water policy: Environmental injustice and peripheral marginalisation
sources.temporal_coverage: Historical and contemporary water-transfer policy, as discussed in 2024
sources.methodology: Qualitative content analysis of policy and government documents, campaigns and Persian-, Kurdish- and English-language secondary material.
sources.limitations: Interpretive analysis; documents and reported examples do not quantify causal effects of individual transfers.

sources.title: The politics of drought in the Middle East, case study from Iran
sources.temporal_coverage: Recent drought politics, compared across two provinces in a 2025 study
sources.methodology: Comparative qualitative case analysis of drought politics in Isfahan and Hamedan.
sources.limitations: The author notes limited prior research and calls for further regional and media-perception analysis.

claims.paraphrase: Severe water scarcity preceded the July 2021 protests in Khuzestan, where residents protested shortages and deteriorating water conditions.
claims.limitations: The report does not establish climate change as the sole or proximate cause of the protests.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: The report states that severe water scarcity sparked the 2021 protests; it identifies political and socioeconomic conditions as part of the context.

claims.locator: Publisher summary, Why does it matter?
claims.paraphrase: The summary says government coercion and short-term remedies can exacerbate Khuzestan's water crisis and set up further turmoil.
claims.limitations: Publisher summary only; the full report's causal discussion was not used.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: The summary states that coercive and short-term responses can exacerbate the underlying water crisis and further turmoil.

claims.locator: Abstract; sections on inter-basin transfers and peripheral regions
claims.paraphrase: The author argues that transfers from western and southern donor basins toward central Iran have damaged donor-area water systems and heightened center-periphery tensions.
claims.limitations: Author's qualitative interpretation of policy and secondary materials; no transfer-level causal estimates.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: The author explicitly characterizes transfer policy as contributing to environmental injustice and conflictual state-periphery relations.

claims.locator: Sections on Chaharmahal and Bakhtiari and Khuzestan
claims.paraphrase: The article reports that more than 200 villages in Chaharmahal and Bakhtiari relied on tanker water, while Khuzestan faced salinity, water scarcity and loss of date palms.
claims.limitations: Figures and examples are reported through the article's document review and cited sources.

claims.locator: Discussion of water transfers and protest
claims.paraphrase: The author reports that disagreements over inter-basin transfers and their perceived inequities have accompanied local protest and sociopolitical tension.
claims.limitations: The article synthesizes reported tensions; it does not estimate the independent contribution of transfers.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: The author associates transfer-related environmental injustice and water conflict with peripheral marginalization and protest.

claims.locator: Comparative findings on Isfahan and Hamedan
claims.paraphrase: The study contrasts farmer mobilization around drought and water allocation in Isfahan with an absence of comparable protest in Hamedan.
claims.limitations: Comparative qualitative case analysis; does not show that drought alone explains the differing protest patterns.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: The study examines how drought and political responses relate to farmer protest, with different patterns in Isfahan and Hamedan.

claims.paraphrase: The author argues that drought-related water problems can reduce political trust and that weak water-governance responses shape local contention.
claims.limitations: The paper identifies a qualitative relationship and notes the need for further regional evidence.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: The author states that drought-associated water problems can undermine trust in authorities and intensify political dissatisfaction.

claims.paraphrase: From 2008-2018, levels declined in 53% of eastern and northeastern aquifers; drawdown reached 33 metres around Dezful and Andimeshk.
claims.limitations: Measurements are historical and do not establish current aquifer conditions.

claims.locator: Abstract; results, groundwater quality and regional distribution
claims.paraphrase: The study finds groundwater quality generally declines southward; 27% of sampled groundwater was unsuitable for agriculture, with better-quality aquifers concentrated north and east.
geographies: Northern, eastern, central and southern Khuzestan
claims.limitations: Study sample and data cover 2008-2018; percentages refer to sampled groundwater, not residents.

search_audit.query: Iran provincial climate vulnerability groundwater subnational World Bank report drought wetlands
search_audit.outcome: Found basin, aquifer and province-level evidence for Khuzestan, Isfahan, Hamedan and Chaharmahal and Bakhtiari; existing bank sources cover additional wetlands.

search_audit.query: Iran climate water scarcity protests conflict mediators source report province primary research
search_audit.outcome: Indexed Khuzestan summary and two full studies link water scarcity or drought governance with contention; climate is not treated as a sole cause.

search_audit.query: Iran sanctions conflict climate adaptation institutional capacity environment water source report province
search_audit.outcome: Found summary evidence on coercive responses worsening water-related unrest; no accessible primary study was found showing conflict or sanctions directly restricting local adaptation delivery.

search_audit.outcome: Existing bank material covers the Iranian Wetlands Project; no new independently evaluated local resilience outcome was located, and the GCF plan page was blocked.

gaps: The inspected sources cluster around Khuzestan and central/inter-basin water disputes; current original subnational evidence is thinner for other provinces.
Conflict-related restrictions on climate adaptation were not substantiated by an additional accessible primary source in this search batch.
The GCF adaptation document and a Lake Urmia article search were blocked, so no claims from them are included.
